children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 11 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Let me ask you a few questions about your situation to determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now let me ask:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you paying at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do contribute towards his upkeep - I help with things like his clothes, school expenses, and other things he needs. I pay about £26 a week towards his costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a clarifying question:

**Does Alex live with someone else (such as his other parent, a relative, or friend), and do you know if that person is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with his mum. As far as I know, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Just to confirm a few more details:

**How long has Alex been living with his mum - has it been more than 8 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been much longer than that - he's been living with her for quite a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Based on the information you've provided, let me make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

You've told me that:
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with his mum (not with you)
- He's been living with his mum for longer than 8 weeks
- You contribute about £26 per week towards his upkeep
- His mum is not claiming Child Benefit for him (as far as you know)

According to the rules, you can continue to get Child Benefit for a child who lives with someone else if you contribute to their upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment. The current Child Benefit rate is approximately £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, and you're contributing about £26 per week.

However, I need to clarify one important point: **Is anyone else (particularly Alex's mum) actually claiming Child Benefit for Alex currently? Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his mum isn't claiming it. Nobody else is getting Child Benefit for him.

Here's why:

✓ **Alex meets the age requirement** - He's 11 years old (under 16)
✓ **You meet the residency requirement** - You live in the UK
✓ **You meet the responsibility requirement** - Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing approximately £26 per week towards his upkeep, which is at least equal to the Child Benefit payment (around £25.60 per week for an eldest/only child)
✓ **No one else is claiming** - Alex's mum is not claiming Child Benefit for him, and only one person can claim for each child

**What to do next:**
You can make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Keep records of your contributions towards his upkeep (receipts, bank transfers, etc.) as you may need to demonstrate these contributions.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you can still claim the benefit.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
